acceptance_criteria: JooqDeviceRepository.deleteDevice uses target_device_id and correct FK cascade sequence without throwing column or FK constraint errors
SecurityWebMvcConfig.EXPLICITLY_UNGATED_ROUTES includes GET /error and POST /error so internal exceptions are not masked as ACTION_MAPPING_REQUIRED 403 errors
DeviceRegistryPanel.tsx displays delete error notifications without collapsing the device list view into an unrecoverable empty state
All service tests (:service:test), persistence tests (:persistence:test), and frontend CI (:frontendCi) pass
Privacy gate (python3 scripts/repository_privacy_check.py) passes with zero findings

baseline.observed: Attempting to delete a device triggers HTTP 500 in JooqDeviceRepository due to 'column device_id does not exist' on jobs table. The unhandled exception is dispatched to /error which is rejected with 403 ACTION_MAPPING_REQUIRED by GateChainInterceptor because /error is not in EXPLICITLY_UNGATED_ROUTES.
baseline.what_exists: JooqDeviceRepository.deleteDevice currently queries 'from jobs where device_id = ?' and references job_steps incorrectly instead of 'target_device_id' and 'job_step_attempt.job_id'. Jobs table also has reciprocal FK reconciliation_ref to job_reconciliation requiring reconciliation_ref = null first. SecurityWebMvcConfig lacks /error in EXPLICITLY_UNGATED_ROUTES.

invariants: Strict role-based action gating (DEVICE_DELETE requires role:onboarding_admin)
Zero role string literals in frontend (NoRoleConditionalRenderingInFrontendTest)
Transactional cascaded deletion to ensure referential integrity
Fail-closed security: unmapped routes remain rejected except for explicitly ungated error endpoints
report.objective: Fix SQL schema column names and FK cascade order in JooqDeviceRepository.deleteDevice, and ungate /error route in SecurityWebMvcConfig to prevent ACTION_MAPPING_REQUIRED masking on backend exceptions.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Fixing SQL cascade schema mismatch and Spring error route gating

requirements: In JooqDeviceRepository.java deleteDevice: 1) update jobs set reconciliation_ref = null where target_device_id = {0}; 2) delete from job_step_attempt where job_id in (select job_id from jobs where target_device_id = {0}); 3) delete from job_steps where job_id in (select job_id from jobs where target_device_id = {0}); 4) delete from job_reconciliation where job_id in (select job_id from jobs where target_device_id = {0}); 5) delete from device_configuration_run where device_id = {0}; 6) delete from device_inventory_run where device_id = {0}; 7) delete from configuration_artefact where device_id = {0}; 8) delete from cp_inventory_projection where device_id = {0}; 9) delete from configuration_notification where device_id = {0}; 10) delete from backup_artefact where device_id = {0}; 11) delete from backup_endpoint_ineligibility where device_id = {0}; 12) delete from jobs where target_device_id = {0}; 13) delete from endpoints where device_id = {0}; 14) delete from devices where device_id = {0}.
In SecurityWebMvcConfig.java: add 'GET /error' and 'POST /error' to EXPLICITLY_UNGATED_ROUTES.
In DeviceRegistryPanel.tsx: handle delete error gracefully so that delete error does not overwrite the device registry list view with an empty error panel.
Run ./ui2/gradlew -p ui2 :persistence:test :service:test :frontendCi to verify all tests pass.
